content.value_statement: Performance changes often add complexity without proving user impact. This skill guides measurement, focused fixes, verification, and regression protection across application layers.
actual_capabilities: Establishes repeatable baselines using synthetic measurements and real user monitoring.
Maps frontend and backend symptoms to likely bottlenecks and appropriate profiling methods.
Reviews N+1 queries, pagination, indexes, connection pools, caching, images, rendering, and bundle size.
Defines Core Web Vitals targets and practical performance budgets.
Compares before and after results while accounting for measurement variance.
Designs CI gates and field monitoring to detect performance regressions.
limitations: It does not provide measurements without access to the application and representative workloads.
Example thresholds require adjustment for product requirements, infrastructure, and user conditions.
Database recommendations require validation against real query plans and production data distributions.
Optimization changes still require functional tests and review for correctness.

use_cases.title: Improve Web Vitals
use_cases.description: Diagnose poor LCP, INP, or CLS and prioritize measurable frontend changes.

use_cases.title: Reduce API Latency
use_cases.description: Trace slow endpoints through queries, connection pools, caching, and application code.

use_cases.title: Prevent Regressions
use_cases.description: Define budgets, repeatable benchmarks, CI gates, and production monitoring for critical user metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Find the First Measurement
prompt_templates.prompt: My application feels slow during [workflow]. Help me choose one user-facing metric, a representative test condition, and a repeatable baseline.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Bottleneck
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these measurements and traces for [workflow]: [evidence]. Identify the likely bottleneck, explain the evidence, and propose the smallest useful experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed performance change: [change]. Compare baseline and result data, check correctness risks, account for variance, and recommend keep or revert.

prompt_templates.title: Design Regression Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a performance protection plan for [system]. Define budgets, benchmark conditions, sample strategy, CI enforcement, field alerts, and an investigation workflow.

output_examples.input: The product page has an LCP of 4.3 seconds on mobile. The hero image is 1.8 MB and begins loading late.
output: Primary metric: mobile p75 LCP under 2.5 seconds.
Likely bottleneck: the oversized, late-discovered LCP image.
Experiment: resize responsive variants, use modern formats, and raise discovery priority.
Verification: repeat the same mobile test and confirm layout and image quality.

output_examples.input: An endpoint performs one task query and 80 owner queries. Its p95 latency is 920 milliseconds.
output: Likely bottleneck: an N+1 query pattern.
Experiment: fetch owners through one join or batched query.
Success condition: fewer queries and a meaningful p95 reduction with unchanged results.
Regression control: add a query-count assertion for the endpoint.

output_examples.input: Memoization reduced average interaction latency by 3 percent, while repeated runs vary by 5 percent.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: revert. The observed change is smaller than normal variance, so the optimization has no demonstrated benefit.

best_practices: Measure the same user-facing metric before and after each isolated change.
Validate performance gains only when functional tests remain green.
Record successful and reverted experiments with conditions and results.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize from intuition without profiling evidence.
Do not combine several changes into one measurement.
Do not keep complexity when improvement remains within measurement noise.

faq.question: Does this skill run profiling tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides tool selection and analysis, but execution depends on the available environment and user approval.

faq.question: Can it optimize frontend and backend systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers rendering, assets, bundles, APIs, queries, connection pools, and caching.

faq.question: Which Core Web Vitals does it address?
faq.answer: It addresses LCP, INP, and CLS through measurement, diagnosis, focused changes, and monitoring.

faq.question: Will every suggested optimization improve performance?
faq.answer: No. Each suggestion is a hypothesis that must exceed measurement variance and preserve correctness.

faq.question: Does it support database tuning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers query plans, N+1 patterns, pagination, indexes, selectivity, and connection pool sizing.

faq.question: How does it prevent regressions?
faq.answer: It recommends repeatable budgets in CI and field monitoring for the user-facing metric.
